newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians burn U.S. envoy in effigy in W Bank.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians burn U.S. envoy in effigy in W Bank.

text.p: Thousands of Palestinians took to the streets on Tuesday and burned in effigy U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross dressed as an ultra-Orthodox Jew and holding a baby doll resembling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Witnesses said an estimated 10,000 Palestinians marched in the West Bank town of Nablus chanting slogans condemning Israel and the United States and praising the Palestinian Authority for refusing to make political concessions under pressure.
"This is a message to Ross. Stop U.S. bias towards Israel and stop pressuring the Palestinian Authority to make concessions to Israel," one protester said.
Masked youths burned a dummy of Ross, now visiting Israel, portrayed as an ultra-Orthodox Jew holding a Netanyahu doll. Protesters also ignited American and Israeli flags.

Ross was sent to the region this week to restore security contacts between Palestinians and Israelis after a twin suicide attack on July 30 killed 16 people, including two Arab bombers, in an Israeli market.
PLO officials said they have come under Israeli and U.S. pressure to crack down on Moslem militants.

Israel and the United States have said Arafat needs to do more to curb militants. Arafat has insisted he was combatting violence and accused Israel of using the bombing as a pretext to weaken his Authority and scrap peace moves.
Arafat has said a random crackdown on Islamists could spark civil war between Palestinians.

The march was jointly organised by Palestinian factions that both oppose and support PLO-Israel peace deals, including Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's Fatah mainstream and the militant Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas.
"We hold Netanyahu's terrorist government responsible for all the racist measures against the Palestinian people," said senior Hamas official Jamal Salim.
Israel sealed off the West Bank and Gaza after the attack and cut off financial transfers to the Palestinian Authority.
Israel says the closure is necessary to prevent further suicide bombings. Palestinians have condemned the siege as collective punishment and warned of an "explosion".
"Only just peace brings security for Israel and not its collective punishments," said Fatah official Amin Maqboul.
Salim said the demonstration was to show the world that the Palestinian people backed the "position of the Palestinian Authority which rejects American and Israeli dictates."
